trigger: A single misconfigured regular expression deployed to the Web Application Firewall (WAF).
detection: Automated monitoring alerted on a massive spike in CPU utilization across global edge servers.
impact: Global HTTP/HTTPS traffic passing through Cloudflare returned 502 Bad Gateway errors, affecting millions of websites.
fix: Executed a global WAF rule rollback to restore normal CPU levels and traffic routing.

trigger: A valid customer configuration change triggered a latent software bug in VCL routing.
detection: Internal automated monitoring and customer reports flagged widespread 503 Service Unavailable errors.
impact: 85% of Fastly's global network returned 503 errors, taking down major news outlets, Reddit, Twitch, and gov.uk.
fix: Identified the faulty configuration, disabled it globally, and deployed a permanent software patch.

trigger: A routine maintenance command unintentionally disconnected all Facebook data centers from the global internet backbone.
detection: Automated internal monitoring failed because DNS and internal tools were hosted on the disconnected network; engineers noticed immediately.
impact: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Oculus became completely unreachable worldwide, and internal badge access systems failed.
fix: Engineers physically accessed the data center servers to reset the routers and restore BGP advertisements.

trigger: An engineer accidentally ran rm -rf on the production primary database directory instead of the secondary replica during heavy load.
detection: Engineers immediately realized the command was executed on the wrong terminal window and halted the deletion.
impact: Approximately 300 GB of live production database data (issues, merge requests, snippets) was lost, and GitLab.com was offline for 18 hours.
fix: Restored the database from a 6-hour-old LVM snapshot found on a staging server and rebuilt replication.

trigger: An authorized engineer executed a command with an incorrect parameter, removing far more S3 billing subsystem servers than intended.
detection: Automated alarms triggered due to elevated S3 API error rates in the US-EAST-1 region.
impact: Amazon S3 experienced high error rates in Northern Virginia, disrupting major websites, Slack, Trello, and AWS status dashboards.
fix: Performed a full restart of the S3 index and placement subsystems, which required lengthy integrity checks.

trigger: A massive post-holiday login surge overwhelmed AWS Transit Gateway bandwidth limits during network auto-scaling.
detection: Automated health checks detected elevated packet loss and connection timeouts across Slack API endpoints.
impact: Users worldwide were unable to connect to Slack, send messages, or load channels on the first workday of 2021.
fix: Manually adjusted AWS Transit Gateway routing tables and provisioned additional network capacity.

trigger: An automated configuration change intended for a small group of servers was accidentally applied to multiple regions, shutting down physical networking.
detection: Internal monitoring systems alerted on widespread network congestion and loss of connectivity in US-East regions.
impact: Google Cloud, YouTube, Gmail, Snapchat, and Discord suffered severe latency and downtime across the US East Coast.
fix: Engineers manually bypassed broken control planes to restore physical network links and revert the bad configuration.

trigger: Routine optical network maintenance caused a 43-second connectivity loss between US East and West Coast data centers, triggering an automated database failover.
detection: Automated database health monitors detected split-brain state and replication lag across MySQL clusters.
impact: GitHub displayed stale data, webhooks failed, and GitHub Pages builds were paused for over 24 hours to prevent data loss.
fix: Restored primary database clusters from backups, reconciled inconsistent writes, and synced replication queues.

trigger: A high-volume database migration caused lock contention on a primary database cluster handling live API traffic.
detection: Automated API latency and error rate monitors paged the on-call infrastructure team within minutes.
impact: Live payment processing, checkout flows, and dashboard requests failed or timed out for merchants globally.
fix: Aborted the migration, shed non-critical background database queries, and scaled read replicas.

trigger: An engineer entered an incorrect BGP routing rule to relieve backbone congestion in Atlanta, accidentally routing all global backbone traffic through a single router.
detection: Automated network telemetry immediately alerted on 100% link saturation and packet drops across backbone links.
impact: Roughly 50% of Cloudflare's global traffic dropped, causing widespread outages for Discord, Shopify, and Peloton.
fix: Removed the faulty BGP routing policy in Atlanta to redistribute traffic evenly across the global network.

trigger: A faulty maintenance script executed with the wrong list of IDs, permanently deleting entire customer cloud sites instead of deprecated legacy apps.
detection: Customer support tickets and automated synthetic monitoring alerted engineers to missing Jira and Confluence instances.
impact: 775 enterprise customers lost access to Jira, Confluence, and Opsgenie for up to two weeks.
fix: Built custom recovery tooling to manually restore individual customer databases, attachments, and search indexes from encrypted backups.

trigger: A malformed Rapid Response Content configuration file (Channel File 291) triggered an out-of-bounds memory read in the Windows kernel driver.
detection: Immediate global reports of Windows Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) boot loops across enterprise machines.
impact: Over 8.5 million Windows devices crashed globally, grounding airlines and disrupting hospitals, banks, and emergency services.
fix: Reverted the faulty content update and issued manual Safe Mode recovery instructions to delete the corrupted system file.

trigger: An automated key rotation process removed an active public signing key used by Azure Active Directory before all services had transitioned.
detection: Automated authentication failure alerts triggered across Azure AD and Microsoft 365 services.
impact: Users globally could not sign in to Microsoft Teams, Office 365, Xbox Live, or Azure management portals.
fix: Rolled back the key metadata update and refreshed cached signing keys across global identity edge nodes.

trigger: A backend authentication service experienced cascading timeouts after a routine configuration change.
detection: Automated alerting flagged a sudden drop in active streaming sessions and a spike in HTTP 500 errors.
impact: Millions of users were unexpectedly logged out of Spotify and unable to log back in or stream music.
fix: Reverted the configuration change and throttled login retries to allow backend identity databases to recover.

trigger: A secondary database cluster failed, causing a thundering herd of retry traffic that overwhelmed the primary Cassandra cluster.
detection: Automated API latency monitors and real-time message delivery alerts fired within two minutes of the initial spike.
impact: Users could not send messages, join voice channels, or load server lists across desktop and mobile apps.
fix: Enabled aggressive rate limiting on client reconnects, restarted overloaded Cassandra nodes, and drained message queues.

trigger: An underlying cloud provider network disruption isolated primary Kafka message brokers from consumer services.
detection: External synthetic monitoring and backup alerting systems notified PagerDuty's incident commanders.
impact: Incident notifications, SMS alerts, and phone call escalations were delayed or failed to trigger for engineering teams.
fix: Failed over core event-processing pipelines to a secondary AWS region and cleared the backlog of queued alerts.

trigger: A Kubernetes control plane upgrade caused internal service discovery DNS records to become stale across core microservices.
detection: Automated edge error monitors detected a 100% spike in HTTP 503 responses on reddit.com.
impact: Reddit's website, mobile apps, and API were completely offline globally for over five hours.
fix: Rolled back the Kubernetes upgrade, flushed stale internal DNS caches, and restarted core API pods.

trigger: A Redis cache cluster failover caused a sudden cache stampede against core MySQL storefront databases.
detection: Automated checkout conversion rate monitors and database CPU alerts paged the on-call site reliability team.
impact: Online storefronts failed to load and customers could not complete checkouts across thousands of merchants.
fix: Warm-loaded critical Redis keys, enabled circuit breakers on heavy queries, and restored database read capacity.

trigger: A routine deployment updated an internal billing service configuration with an invalid connection string, causing synchronous timeouts.
detection: Automated alerts detected a sharp drop in outbound SMS and voice call completion rates.
impact: Programmable SMS, voice calls, and two-factor authentication codes failed for customers globally.
fix: Rolled back the billing service deployment and bypassed non-essential billing checks during message routing.

trigger: Attackers compromised stolen OAuth tokens issued to third-party GitHub integrators used by Heroku.
detection: GitHub security monitoring identified unauthorized repository downloads using Heroku OAuth tokens.
impact: Heroku revoked all GitHub OAuth tokens, breaking automated CI/CD deploys for thousands of customer apps.
fix: Rotated credentials, audited access logs, and rebuilt a hardened GitHub OAuth integration.
